newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Confidence in Hong Kong's prosperity rising-survey.
newsitem.headline: Confidence in Hong Kong's prosperity rising-survey.

text.p: People in Hong Kong are growing increasingly confident the territory will remain prosperous under Chinese control, a survey released on Friday showed.

Local broadcaster Asia Television (ATV) said 80 percent of 552 people surveyed this week were confident Hong Kong would remain prosperous after June 30 when British rule ends and China takes control of the territory.
ATV, which commissioned the survey, said confidence in Hong Kong's future prosperity had risen 15 percentage points since a similar survey in January.

Some 70 percent of respondents said they would remain in Hong Kong after the handover, up six points from January, ATV said. Forty-three percent said they would make long-term investments in the territory, it added.

"The next six months would be a politically sensitive time. If there are moves to threaten people's freedoms...confidence will decline," Ming Sing of Hong Kong's City University was quoted by ATV as saying.
He added that the recent surge in confidence was partly due to a decision by the territory's future leader Tung Chee-hwa to retain all principal government officials after the handover.
